note.label: You Are Hated And In Hell

precepts.text: Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities. For whom he did foreknow. You only have I known.
precepts.point: Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified. He shall be glorified in his Son.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” What is good about all the evil we have been watching? All of it is good, because the Lord has been warning our people, the twelve tribes, in the Bible for centuries, and we have not listened, not repented, not returned to him; we have gone into strange religions and worshipped a strange God we think is Jesus Christ. All things includes the things we think are bad for us. There is a divine purpose behind it. We are the called according to his purpose.

“For whom he did foreknow”. Foreknow means knew from the past. Go back to the Old Testament: who did he foreknow? Amos answers: “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. For whom he did foreknow: you only have I known. The twelve tribes of Israel.

“therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”. Because he knew us, he punished us, and the punishment itself is part of the all things that work together for good. It is his warning to return.

“he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son”. Predestinated who? The twelve tribes of Israel, whom he is transforming into the image of Christ, his Son, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. We are the ones being justified. Not all nations on the planet. Paul is not saying everybody on the planet is going to be justified. Nope. He is getting that from what we are reading right there.
precepts.point: Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified. He shall be glorified in his Son.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified”. Here is that word again, predestinate. And who is justified? Isaiah: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

We are the ones being justified, not all nations on the planet. Paul is not saying everybody on the planet is going to be justified. He did not make things up and pull them out of the sky; he is getting that from what Isaiah wrote.

“and whom he justified, them he also glorified”. The seed of Israel justified in the Lord “shall glory”, and he shall be glorified in his Son.

That is why Paul goes on: “If God be for us, who can be against us?” Who can conquer us, who can destroy us? Nobody on this planet, no matter what comes our way. The seed of Israel, called and justified in the Lord, are more than conquerors through him that loved us, and nothing shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

precepts.text: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God. Not the whole world: the Israelites are the children of God. The Bible bears witness with our spirit that we are them children.
precepts.point: And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. The curses is the sign: if our spirit resonates with the signs in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and Genesis 49, we going to realize that we are the Israelites. And for a wonder: we're supposed to be wondering how the greatest people on earth got so low. It's going to be upon our seed until Christ's return.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”. I don't care what country you are in, what state, what continent: these curses are following us. That's why we're getting shot down in the streets and killed left and right; the Most High has to do something to wake us back up. We are a destroyed nation, and we haven't understood that yet.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”. The curses are the sign. That is how we know we are the Israelites: the Bible gives us the signs to look out for, in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and in Genesis 49, and if our spirit resonates with those signs, we are going to realize that we are the Israelites.

That is Romans 8:16: “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”. That we, the Israelites, are the children of God. Not the whole world. The spirit itself, the Bible, bears witness with our spirit that we are those children.

And “for a wonder”: we are supposed to be wondering what happened. We are the greatest people on earth; how did we get so low? It will be upon our seed for ever, upon our children until Christ's return. Brothers want to argue the trinity while our people are being killed, holding the name Israel and refusing everything that goes with it. The sign is on us, and the spirit bears witness with ours: we are Israel, and we have to come back to the Lord.

precepts.text: You only have I known of all the families of the earth. So you know it ain't no church that he's talking about. No Presbyterian, no Catholic, all that garbage. Therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities: so we were punished.
precepts.point: To be conformed to the image of his Son: he's going to transform us, the 12 tribes, into the image of his Son Christ, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“For whom he did foreknow”. Foreknow means knew from the past. Who did God know from the past? Everybody? The church? No. That has to be stressed, especially on the street, because people are so brainwashed with supersessionism, replacement theology, that they say foreknow means everybody in the church.

Amos settles it: “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. The family God knew is the family he brought up out of Egypt, the children of Israel. So it is no church he is talking about: no Presbyterian, no Catholic, all that garbage.

“therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”. Because he knew us, we were punished.

Paul could have said Judah and Israel plainly, as he does in Hebrews and in Romans 9, but in many of his epistles he uses other words for the 12 tribes. “whom he did foreknow” is one of them: the 12 tribes, the only family on earth he has known.

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified. The only ones being justified is all the seed of Israel. It's not talking about the Catholics, not the Jehovah's Witnesses, all those false religions.
precepts.point: To be conformed to the image of his Son: he's going to transform us, the 12 tribes, into the image of his Son Christ, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“whom he called, them he also justified”. Who is being justified? Isaiah answers: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The only ones being justified are all the seed of Israel. It is not talking about the Catholics, not the Jehovah's Witnesses, not any of those false religions.

That is why there is predestination in the Bible. People love to say there is no such thing, but there is, for the 12 tribes of Israel. We were his people in the past, we are going to be his people today and forevermore; we are predestined to be his chosen forever. Whether we as individuals make it or not is up to each individual.

And “whom he justified, them he also glorified”: the seed of Israel that is justified in the Lord “shall glory.” The whole chain of Romans 8:29-30, foreknown, predestinated, called, justified and glorified, runs through the seed of Israel, whom God will transform into the image of his Son, Christ, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

precepts.text: Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called. So he's not calling all nations on the planet Earth. He's only calling Israel. He's not calling Catholics, Jehovah's Witnesses, Baptists. All that goes back to replacement theology, which came about through the Catholic church, then the Protestant church that many of us grew up in, that teach the same thing.
precepts.point: To be conformed to the image of his Son: he's going to transform us, the 12 tribes, into the image of his Son Christ, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. Who did he call? “Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.” Jacob and Israel are his called.

So he is not calling all nations on the planet earth. He is only calling Israel. He is not calling Catholics, Jehovah's Witnesses, Baptists. The teaching that the called are everybody in the church all goes back to replacement theology, which came about through the Catholic church, and then the Protestant church that many of us grew up in, which teaches the same thing.

Put Amos, Isaiah 45 and Isaiah 48 together and Romans 8:29-30 opens up: the ones he foreknew, the ones he called, the ones he justified are the 12 tribes of Israel, predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son.

precepts.text: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, which is Christ: waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. We want our godhood back. We want rulership back, dominion back; we want to reign on this planet like we once did.
precepts.point: To loose those that are appointed to death: he said he is going to loose those appointed to death.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Solomon saw “the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power.” They have the guns, the nuclear weapons, the court system; they have it all, and we have nothing. But the psalm says the Lord looked down from heaven “To hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death.” We are the prisoner. You know what it is like to be the son of God and be in prison: in a weak body, ruled and dominated by a wicked race of people, subject to their laws.

Paul hears the same groaning: “For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.” Just like we groan, all creation groans.

“And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit”: the firstfruits of the Spirit is Christ. “even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.”

That redemption of the body is what the prisoner groans for. We want our godhood back. We want rulership back, dominion back; we want to reign on this planet like we once did. That is the loosing of those appointed to death that the Lord looked down from heaven to bring.

precepts.text: As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Paul is quoting Psalms 44:22: that is why he always said bring the books and the parchments, because his letters referenced things already written.
precepts.point: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger: at one time we knew the white man was our enemy. Now we see him as our avenger, our helper, our bosom buddy. A few decades ago he was your enemy; now he is your lover? It makes no sense.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Paul writes: “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.” That is prophecy right there. And where is it written? In this psalm: “Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen”, and “Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.”

So when Paul was writing Romans 8:36, where do you think he got it? From Psalms. That is why he always said, bring the books and the parchments: the letters he was going to write would reference things already written in the Old Testament.

The sheep appointed for meat, scattered among the heathen, is Deuteronomy 28:64 fulfilled. God sold us for nought; he was not looking for financial gain when he allowed us to be sold. And Paul carried the same understanding into the New Testament: the people of God would be killed all the day long and counted as sheep for the slaughter. It did not stop with the apostles; it is still happening to our people today.

precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, you are a failure. You ain't nothing. You're going to be the same person you always were. The Bible says: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

Guess what? You can repent. The bottle says you're a failure; the Bible says you can repent and become a new man.

But it starts with acknowledging it: I'm an alcoholic. I'm a fornicator, an adulterer, a liar, a thief; I deal with envy, covetousness, idolatry. That is where the change happens. And acknowledging it is not enough; you have to work on fixing those things. You can't say, I'm an alcoholic, and keep going out drinking.

No condemnation belongs to those who walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. The man chained to the bottle is walking after the flesh; the man who casts his burden on the Lord and walks in the Spirit is free of the condemnation the bottle keeps whispering over him.

precepts.text: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. That is what "Israel shall be heir unto them that were his heirs" jumps to.
precepts.point: Then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.” What does that mean? Romans 8 jumps right to it: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

We are joint-heirs with Christ. Ammon made itself heir to Gad, inheriting his cities while Israel was carried away. But Israel is the heir of God, and in that day Israel shall be heir unto them that took his inheritance.

The condition is that we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified together. The suffering comes first, the inheritance after, just as Gad lost his cities and the Lord promises to give them back.

precepts.text: What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death. The fruit of the things you now realize were sinful behavior ends in death. He is dealing with the carnality.
precepts.point: To be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. Notice it is not just life, it is peace. You know why some of you still have so much drama in your lives? Because you are not applying this. You have no peace because you are trying to seek peace in things that are not God. The Bible talks about God's perfect peace, the peace of God which passeth all understanding: it will overcome anything you are dealing with. If it does not seem to work for you, you are still not applying what you need to apply.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
“For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh”. Where your heart is, there will your treasure be: if you are after the flesh, you are going to mind the things of the flesh. “For to be carnally minded is death”. If you stay in that carnal mind, that is death.

Romans 6 goes with it: “What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed?” That is the fruit of the things you now realize were sinful behavior. “for the end of those things is death”. The end of the things you should be ashamed of is death. Paul is dealing with the carnality.

So the death of Romans 8:6 is not a mystery: it is the fruit of minding the flesh. The things we once did in the flesh bore nothing but shame, and their end is death.

Then read Romans 8:5 again with that in mind: “but to be spiritually minded is life and peace”. Notice it is not just life; it is peace. Some of us still have so much drama in our lives because we are not applying this, seeking peace in things that are not God.

When we meditate day and night on the Lord, we build up our trust in him. That is what the second generation had to do in the wilderness that the first generation did not.

You know why some of you still have so much drama in your lives? Because you are not applying this. You have no peace because you are trying to seek peace in things that are not God. The Bible talks about God's perfect peace, the peace of God which passeth all understanding: it will overcome anything you are dealing with. If it does not seem to work for you, you are still not applying what you need to apply.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
To be spiritually minded is life and peace, and Isaiah shows where that peace comes from: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.” This is part of the meditation, the daily feeding. If we are not feeding ourselves, we are being pulled away from God.

When we meditate day and night on the Lord, our mind is stayed on him and we build up our trust in him. That is what the second generation had to do in the wilderness that the first generation did not.

It is heavy, because it says to trust in him. People say, it doesn't work for me; that shows they do not trust in God. It is unbelievable how much goes back to your faith. If you are weak in spirit, your faith is weak too. If your faith is only strong when things are going your way, that is not faith at all; if it is only when things benefit you that you feel confident trusting God, then you do not trust in God.

The peace of God overcomes anything you are dealing with or struggling with. If it does not seem to work for you, you are still not applying it: keep your mind stayed on him and trust him, and he keeps you in perfect peace.

precepts.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, the servant is not greater than his lord. Christ was the example, and we are going to walk the same footsteps; you are going to get punished the same way. It is not going to be easy; it is not supposed to be easy. If our Lord and Master went through it, do you not think that you are going to go through it? If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.
precepts.point: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. And there is a period at the end of that. Nothing should be able to separate you, because you know what is at the end of this: paradise is waiting on us. You are being put in a furnace to be tried and turned into pure gold. Your wicked family turning their back on you? Good. When I came in this truth I got rid of a whole lot of dead weight and useless conversations; the only people that call me now call about the truth. If it is not about the scriptures, do not talk to me; that is beneficial for me and for you.

note.label: Forged by Fire

precepts.why:
Romans 8 says, “He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?” The Most High is trying to give us a kingdom. Christ went through the furnace, and he is doing the same thing with us. We are the ambassadors of Christ: do you think you are not going to go through the same thing? Do you think you are not going to be punished? Yes, you are.

Christ said it himself: “For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you. Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him.” Christ was the example, and we are going to walk the same footsteps. We will be punished the same way he was.

It is not going to be easy, and it is not supposed to be easy. If our Lord and Master went through it, do you not think that you are going to go through it? Do you not think that you deserve to go through it?

“If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.” Knowing that the servant walks where his lord walked, we take the fire as the way to be fixed. That is why all things work together for good to them that love God: the trials are the furnace Christ went through first, and the kingdom is at the end of it.

precepts.text: We know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. We all go through things we don't understand while we're going through them. Whether you're suffering poverty, health problems, eviction, trials, or temptations, endure to the end; there's a purpose.
precepts.point: Only a spiritual man can understand that. Joseph was on another level of understanding: he sat back and reflected on all that happened to him and knew it was God's divine plan. He may not have understood it while he was in the midst of it, but going through the years of plenty and famine he realized his purpose, and God set that whole thing up.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
When Jacob died, Joseph's brethren were afraid: “Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him.” They sent a messenger begging forgiveness, “And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.” Then he said, “Fear not: for am I in the place of God?” “But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.”

Only a spiritual man can understand that. Joseph was on another level of understanding. He sat back and reflected on everything that happened to him, the pit, the slavery, the lie, the dungeon, and knew it was God's divine plan. He may not have understood it while he was in the midst of it, but going through the seven years of plenty and the seven years of famine he realized his purpose. God set that whole thing up.

Paul gives the precept: “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” We all go through things we don't understand while we are going through them, asking why God is doing this to me and nobody else. There is a purpose.

All things means all things: poverty, health problems, eviction, trials, tribulations, temptations, whatever it is. If you love God, you must endure it to the end, as Joseph did, and it will work together for good.

precepts.text: Ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body.
precepts.point: The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ is the firstfruits, and his people are called firstfruits with him: “And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.”

Redemption of what body? The body that we used to have, when we were in the heavens with Christ. That is what we groan and wait for.

We are supposed to be the firstfruits: the crème de la crème, the best of the best, if we would repent in Christ. So the “firstfruits unto the Lord” brought out of Israel’s habitations in Leviticus 23:17 point not only to Christ risen, but to the Israelites who have his Spirit and wait for their redemption.

precepts.text: The earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God; the creature itself shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That's our expectation. So if we know the wages of sin is death, then why sin? Then you're not expecting this. In that day he's going to say, I never knew you; you didn't do what I said to do. How do you expect something you didn't do?
precepts.point: The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. The payment for sin is death. Through Christ is eternal life; isn't that what we're looking for? If we keep the commandments, we are expecting the kingdom.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death”. The payment for sin is death. “but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord”. Through Christ is eternal life, and that is what we are looking for. If we keep the commandments, God says he is going to give us the kingdom, so we are expecting the kingdom.

Romans 8 shows that expectation: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” The creature “was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope”, “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” That is what our expectation is to be: delivered out of bondage into the liberty of the children of God.

Then if we know the wages of sin is death, why sin? If you live in sin you are not expecting this; you know what you are going to get. In that day you will be saying Lord, Lord, and he will say, I don't know you; you didn't do what I said to do. How do you expect something you did not do?

So if your expectation is to be called a son of God in the kingdom, do not let sin reign in this mortal body. The one living a life of sin and thinking he will go to the kingdom is not going; he will be in the lake.

precepts.text: The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered: that part of us that groans to God because we're expecting the kingdom, if we're sincere. All things work together for good to them that love God: if you love God, you are keeping the commandments. Whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son: you're going to measure to the fulness of the stature of Christ in this mortal body, because sin cannot reign in this mortal body. Stop thinking it happens on the other side; whoever couldn't figure out that you cannot live a life of sin and enter the kingdom is going to the lake. A hard word with it: sisters that are married, if you refuse to reverence your husband and live to his guidance in the Lord, no head covering or office covers that. And husbands, if you're not guiding your wife and molding your house in these scriptures, that's on you; you're no wise master builder, and the children pay for it. When a child in a covenant house is deep in uncleanness, something is wrong in that house.
precepts.point: Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead. Because you're expecting the kingdom.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
“Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.” That is the part of us that groans to God because we are expecting the kingdom, if we are sincere. We are asking God to deal with us: I want the kingdom, I don't want to come up short, Lord, please preserve me, help me. Then let the word be engrafted in your mind; he is telling you what to do.

“And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.”

“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God”. If you love God, you are keeping the commandments. It works for good to those keeping the commandments, those that have the word engrafted in them, “the called according to his purpose.”

“For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son”. Those that followed him before will follow him again; they are predestinated. You are going to be conformed to that image and measure to the fulness of the stature of Christ in this mortal body, because sin cannot reign in this mortal body. Stop thinking it is going to happen on the other side. Whoever could not figure out that you cannot live a life of sin and go to the kingdom is not going; they are going to be in the lake.

A hard word goes with it. Sisters that are married: if you refuse to serve your husband, look at him as your lord and obey him, down to the little things he tells you to do, you are not going, no matter how many head covers you wear or what offices you hold. If Jesus told you, you would do it. And husbands, if you are not guiding your wives in these scriptures and showing them how to be that woman, that is your fault; you are no wise master builder, having expectations while not molding them. Then the children are cursed. When a twelve-year-old in the house is deep in gay porn, something is wrong in that house, something is wrong with those parents.

precepts.text: If ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: when we obey the elements of the flesh and make the bottle an outlet, the end of that road is always death. But if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live; for as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.
precepts.point: Captain's teaching: it is not a sin to drink, but when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good, which is God's laws.

note.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

precepts.why:
It is not a sin to drink. But when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation; it is not to be used in that manner. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome these things.

“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die”. To live after the flesh is to obey the elements of the flesh: going to the bottle and making that the outlet. The end of that road is always death, just as Habakkuk 2:12 shows that there is always an evil road, and at the end of it you find death.

“but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live”. That is where we are. The drinking problem in this land is a quarter trillion dollars, but the commandments fix all of that.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” That is how we are to be. So we should not be overcome with that evil; we have to overcome that evil with good, and the good is God's laws.

precepts.text: To be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. The carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God. When you are spiritually minded you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean always being buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers want to hold on to that rival feeling, waiting to get back at the brother; that is the carnal mind.
precepts.point: For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears: hold on to that bitter spirit and you will find that same place of no repentance. In that day it will be too late; the judgment is set.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Esau was a man of the field and a profane person: his religion is sin. Paul gives the name for that mind: “For to be carnally minded is death.” To be carnally minded is to be Edomite minded, the profane mind. It is death, and that is why he is called the son of perdition.

“but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” When you are spiritually minded, you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean we always have to be buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers turn a brother into an enemy like a rival team in sports, stay pumped up against him and hold on to that feeling, waiting to get back at him. That is the carnal mind. Stay in the spirit.

“Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God.” The Edomite mind, the mind of the spirit of Cain, goes against God and is not subject to his law.

So there are the children of God and the children of the devil, with no in between: either the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The bitter spirit that holds a grudge against a brother is the carnal mind of Esau, and it leads to the same death and rejection he found.

precepts.text: The earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. Everybody is waiting for our manifestation to be called the sons of God.
precepts.point: The earth was filled with violence through them: that them goes back to Cain's seed. Cain's seed was influencing everybody; what we read in Genesis 4 about Cain's children affected all people on the earth. So God told Noah, Make thee an ark of gopher wood.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Everybody is waiting for our manifestation, for us to be called the sons of God. That is the same name Genesis 6 gives, which settles who the sons of God were: men of our people, not angels.

With that understanding, Genesis 6 reads plainly. It says that “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” That spark from God that we had produced renowned and powerful men on the earth, and they were battling the giants.

But we were not righteous; we had already started breaking God's laws inside that city. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” Think of the great cities today, like New York City: murder, wicked music, buying and selling, stealing. It is the same thing going on now that was going on then, down to a married man looking over at other nations' women.

“The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.” God told Noah, “the earth is filled with violence through them”, and that “them” goes back to Cain's seed. What we read in Genesis 4 about Cain's children affected all people on the earth. So God said, “Make thee an ark of gopher wood”. The sons of God were meant to be manifest, but by mixing with Cain's world they were corrupted with it.

precepts.text: What the law could not do in that it was weak through the flesh, God did by sending his Son and condemned sin in the flesh: he ended the condemnation of all twelve tribes by his death.
precepts.point: Ye who were kept under the law are all the children of God by faith in Christ, whether Jew or Greek, bond or free, male or female, the same people in different conditions. If ye be Christ's then are ye Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise, and the promise pertains to Israel; name me one other nation God calls his people in the Old Testament.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” The we is Israel, kept under the law of sacrifice until Christ came on the scene and died for us, the same as Hebrews 9 saying it was imposed until the time of reformation. “Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ”: our mentor, our stepping stone, the placeholder for Christ's body being offered in the end. “that we might be justified by faith”: Christ's death justifies us, not the law of sacrifice.

What was it that could not justify? “For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh”. The law referred to here is animal sacrifice. Weak through the flesh means through our flesh, and it involves the animals as well. “God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh”.

He did away with our condemnation by his own death. As Caiaphas said, it is expedient that one man should die for the people, that the whole nation perish not. Christ ended the condemnation of all twelve tribes by dying on the cross.

So “after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.” Christ has come and gone, and we are all the children of God by faith in Christ, not by animal sacrifice. That was the bewitching earlier in the chapter: that you could be justified without Christ, and all you needed was an animal.

precepts.text: He that despised Moses' law died without mercy: no grace under Moses, and you are not David, Moses or Esther, so do not try it.
precepts.point: There is now no condemnation to them in Christ Jesus who walk after the Spirit: condemnation is the death you got by stoning, fire or the tree for what no animal could atone. The law of the Spirit of life in Christ has made me free, given me liberty, from the law of sin and death: sin under Moses got you certain death without repentance, and that law was weak through the flesh because the people offering were sinful.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus”. The condemnation goes back to the curse on him that continueth not in all things written in the law. Almost all things were purged with blood, not all. There were sins no animal could help you atone for, and if you fell under that, you got condemnation: death. You got stoned to death, set on fire, or hung from a tree.

That is “the law of sin and death”, the law of sacrifice. Hebrews shows it: “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”. He that hated Moses’ law, the law we all agreed to keep, died without mercy. There was no grace under Moses. If you sinned a certain sin against the Lord, you got immediate death. There was no, I’m sorry, I repent, I didn’t mean to. It was death. Condemnation and death are synonymous.

The Most High had mercy on David, on Moses, on Solomon. But you are not David, you are not Solomon, you are not Moses, you are not Esther. Do not even try that, because you will.

“For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh”: the law of sin and death was weak because the people offering the sacrifices were weak and sinful. “The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death”: made me free, given me liberty. By Christ “all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” Under the animals you could not repent of everything; under Christ’s death you can. That is why there is now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.

precepts.text: Whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son. Conform means change. We can see the potential in a brother, but you have to see it yourself; a deacon's job is to push your spirit, not to see it for you.
precepts.point: I do not trust you, because you do not know the scriptures and you have not put in the work, and God who called you does not trust you either. When persecution shows up you will be the first to turn against us, for one piece of silver rather than thirty.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence.” Some of you have no confidence and low self-esteem because you have no fear of God, sitting in the same seat for seven years. Romans shows what God called you for: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

What does it mean to be conformed? To change. We must change to the image of Jesus Christ. Some of you have not changed yet, and we can see it.

We can see the potential on you: this brother has the spirit to do great things in Israel. But you have to see it. My job as a deacon is to push your spirit and to build you up, but no matter how much I build you up, if you cannot see it, I cannot make you see it. You have to get up and see it yourself.

There is a lot of work to do while you are waiting for the kingdom, and the kingdom does not come by observation. When temptation and tribulation come, the one who has not been conformed will run, because mentally and spiritually he is not strong enough to endure it. Being predestinated to be conformed means you have to do the changing.

precepts.text: What the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, through our sin: it could not make the conscience perfect, Hebrews 9:9. That is the weak in weak and beggarly elements.
precepts.point: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years; I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. Colossians 2:16: let no man judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. Ezekiel 45:17 answers both: it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings, and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths, and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and the Pharisees, whose bread and butter was people bringing animals, were trying to win the churches back to temple law, saying to hell with what Christ did. If you need an animal, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?” We know the true God now, not a pagan one, and we are known of God because Christ died for us. Verse 3 said we were in bondage under the elements of the world; verse 9 calls them weak and beggarly elements. It is the same bondage the false brethren of chapter 2 wanted to bring us back into. So what are they?

Some say we keep saying law of sacrifice and it does not say that. But it does call it weak. “For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh”. Weak through the flesh means weak through our sin, through us.

What could the law not do? Hebrews 9:9 says the gifts and sacrifices “could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrificing of animals could not make us perfect. That is what the law could not do, and that is the weak in the weak and beggarly elements.

So God sent his own Son to do what the animals could not, and to turn back to animal sacrifice after knowing God is to desire again to be in bondage.

precepts.text: Whom he did foreknow, knew before, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren; whom he did predestinate, them he also called, the elect of 1 Peter 1:1-2, the strangers scattered in Galatia, elect according to the foreknowledge of God, the chosen generation and holy nation of 1 Peter 2:9; whom he called, them he also justified through the blood of Christ; and whom he justified, them he also glorified, Isaiah 45:25, justified and shall glory. Amos 3:1-3: you only have I known of all the families of the earth, therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities; all nations sin, but God acknowledges only Israel's sins and sent Christ for them, and can two walk together, except they be agreed? Before Adam was made, God knew the nation he would justify and glorify through his Son.
precepts.point: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound: the law was introduced so sin could be understood and exposed, thou shalt not covet, thou shalt not commit adultery, to guide a naturally sinful people. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
“So by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.” Who are the many? Romans 8 answers: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.” Foreknow means knew before. Before Adam was made, God knew the nation he would justify and glorify through his Son.

“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. The called are the elect Peter wrote to, the strangers scattered throughout Galatia and the rest, “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”, “a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation”.

“And whom he called, them he also justified”: justified through the blood of Christ. “And whom he justified, them he also glorified”: as Isaiah says, “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Amos says it plainly: “You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” All nations sin, but God acknowledges only Israel’s sins and sent Christ for them. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” The free gift unto justification of life came upon the people God foreknew.

precepts.text: He that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit. The verse names both the spiritual and the physical man, and that war between them will not end until Christ returns or you die in this.
precepts.point: I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, to give every man according to his ways and the fruit of his doings. Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath on our best behaviour; six days a week nobody here knows what you are doing. The sister in Georgia bowed and said shalom for ten years while carrying on with the Uber Eats driver, and thought she was fooling the Most High.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
“I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.” Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath, and when we come around each other we are on our best behaviour. Six days a week, Sunday to Friday, we do not know where you are or what you are doing. So what are you doing when you are not here? The sister in Georgia bowed, said shalom and happy Sabbath for ten years while carrying on with the Uber Eats driver. She thought she was fooling us, and surely thought she was fooling the Most High. You cannot fool the Most High.

Paul says the same: “And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit”. The one who searches the heart is searching the mind. And that verse tells you there are two: the spiritual and the physical man. There is a war, the spirit against the flesh, wicked against righteous, darkness against light.

That war will never be over until Christ comes back or you die in this. Some want it to be over and ask why there is so much evil in their head. Maybe because you are not reading enough. Brothers who do not know the scriptures will be the ones to betray you, because when they come to him he will fall. Ask yourself when the brother you talk to during the week last talked scripture with you. The Lord searching the heart gives every man according to his ways: not the deacon's way or the bishop's way, but yours. You are your own biggest enemy.

precepts.text: All things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
precepts.point: A brother deported from France for refusing to stop teaching is now in Ghana and doing well. Papers and citizenship can be taken away, so prepare.

note.label: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.why:
“But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.” Every hair on your head is numbered, so nothing can happen to you unless the Lord allows it. Don't be living and rolling in fear, and don't be scared of no damn ICE. A man's going is of the Lord. The spirit of Christ dwells in you; you are valuable.

Paul adds, “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God.” If you love God, whatever happens, even bad things in your life, happens for good. When Aquila and Priscilla were deported, it was for good: they ended up as Paul's helpers teaching the gospel. God had a plan for them.

“To them who are the called according to his purpose.” Every last one of us is called according to God's purpose. None of us knows where our going is or what the Lord has planned for us, but he has a purpose for each of us.

A brother in France was told to stop teaching the word of God or leave. He would not stop, so they labelled him an extremist, refused to renew his papers, and deported him. Right now he is in Ghana, doing good, all praises to the Lord. So don't think papers, a green card or citizenship will protect you; laws are being set up to take them away from those who speak against America or Christianity. If they take your green card and send you back, it is what it is, of the Lord. Don't run, don't cry and lose your dignity; make preparation, and go over there and teach the word, because all things work together for good to them that love God.

precepts.text: Creation waits for the manifestation of the sons of God.
precepts.point: Their children turned into giants and wickedness, and man's days were cut to 120 years.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All creation is waiting for the sons of God, Israel, to be revealed. The sons of God fell in Genesis 6 by judging unjustly, but the plan still stands.

Psalm 82:8: “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.” Psalm 2:8 says to Christ: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” And we are joint heirs: Romans 8:17, “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”. What Christ gets, he gives to us. Revelation 2:26-27: “to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”, “even as I received of my Father.”

Christ has made us “kings and priests” (Revelation 1:6), and Paul says, “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” The saints are the children of Israel, as Psalm 148:14 says. “Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” The angels we will judge are not Michael or Gabriel; they are each other, the twelve tribes, as Christ promised the twelve would sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

That is the manifestation creation is waiting for. We may look like nobody now, but in time we will rule the nations with Christ. All we have to do is endure to the end.

precepts.text: He that overcometh receives power over the nations, to rule them with a rod of iron.
precepts.point: Israel are joint heirs, so the power over the nations given to Christ is given to them.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
In Psalms 2 the Father says to Christ, “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” Christ is going to inherit all these nations and rule the planet.

All that Christ was given, we share, because we are “joint-heirs with Christ”. That is what a joint heir is: what Christ gets, he is going to give to us. Here is the proof: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”.

This is what we read in Psalms 2 that Christ is going to get, but because we are joint heirs, we are going to get it too. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.” The same honor and glory the Father gave to Christ, Christ says, I am going to give you that same power.

All we have to do, brothers, is endure to the end. “If so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together”: he that overcometh and keepeth his works unto the end is the one who receives power over the nations.

precepts.text: Christ hath made us kings and priests.
precepts.point: Israel are joint heirs, so the power over the nations given to Christ is given to them.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Psalms 2 goes on after the Father gives Christ the heathen for his inheritance: “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings”. Who are these kings? Revelation shows you: Christ “hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father”.

That is a message to us, advice and a command: be wise, O ye kings. “Be instructed, ye judges of the earth.” Christ is calling us judges of the earth. We might look like knuckles right now, but just give us time.

Paul says the same thing: “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” And the saints are not everybody who believes on Jesus: “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. The saints are the Israelites, and the Israelites will judge this planet. Christ said the twelve that followed him “shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

So being heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ means being made kings and priests, the rulers and judges of the earth with him. If that is our future, Paul asks, why can we not judge the smallest matters among ourselves now? Be wise, be instructed, and endure.

precepts.text: Creation waits for the sons of God to be revealed and rule the earth rightly.
precepts.point: God brings every work into judgment with every secret thing, good or evil.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Man was put on this earth to rule it with God's commandments, and because we are not doing that, the earth is suffering; we are not in power. The earth was made to receive your direction, men.

Paul shows it: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Expectation means I am expecting something, and earnestly means with a begging type of attitude. The creation is earnestly waiting for the manifestation, and manifestation means the growth: time for us to stop being kids and manifest into men, to get ourselves together. The earth is waiting for the sons of God to manifest into gods, that is, to rule this planet properly.

And righteous women are waiting for that too. The woman is called woman because she is of man, and she is like the earth: you plant your seed in her and she brings forth fruit, but she needs your guidance. She is supposed to revolve around you, and when you are not in rulership she is out of orbit, like a satellite floating in space with no direction. That is why women cry, where are our black men? The father figure in the house got destroyed.

All of it fell apart when we broke the laws of the Most High from the very beginning, when the woman was out of order with her husband. So it is up to us men to fulfil the duty of manhood to fix it: to marry, build a nation, and rule rightly. That is what the whole creation is waiting on.

precepts.text: Creation waits for the manifestation of the sons of God.
precepts.point: I have said ye are gods, but ye shall die like men.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” What do we not know? “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” God judges in the congregation of the gods, and we are those beings that were with Adam in the beginning, ruling and judging this earth. That is the branches and the boughs. “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes”: it was not like that in the beginning. That is what happened after Adam fell.

Paul shows what we are waiting for: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” We have an eternal body in the heavens, the same body we had with Adam in the beginning. After Adam sinned, the Lord appointed that all of us must come on the earth through Adam in the flesh and fight to get the kingdom, the same way Christ came and overcame.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All the creatures are waiting for the sons of God to be manifest. In Genesis we are called the sons of God; we are called the twelve tribes of Israel. “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” We want to be delivered from this corrupted body.

Paul says of us, “even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We want back the body we had in the beginning, before Adam fell. To some this is foolishness; to others it is the power of God. You have to see what the Bible says. That is faith.

precepts.text: Creation shall be delivered into the glorious liberty of the children of God.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee.” Paul shows what that redemption brings: “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.”

The creature itself is you and me. We shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is talking about us being delivered, not just from this body, but from captivity.

It is the same promise as Jeremiah 16: the Lord that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands whither he had driven them, bringing them again into the land he gave their fathers. Isaiah 43 says he will say to the north, Give up, and bring his sons and daughters from the ends of the earth.

So “I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” ends in liberty: the children of God set free from bondage, the captives delivered in the year of jubilee.

precepts.text: Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat: he called the disciples children because they are his children.
precepts.point: Because Christ adopted us, he is our father, and he is no longer the only begotten but the firstborn among many brethren, which is why he taught us to pray our Father.

precepts.point: The matter is by the decree of the watchers, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and giveth it to whomsoever he will and setteth over it the basest of men. That is what we see today, the basest of men ruling the earth.

note.label: Daniel 4: Nebuchadnezzar Abased Until He Knew the Most High Rules

precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” The whole creation is waiting for the sons of God to be manifested. The great tree that fed and sheltered all flesh was hewn down by the decree of the watchers, its stump bound with iron and brass and a beast's heart given to him till seven times passed over him, “to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.”

That is what we see today: the basest of men ruling the earth. The Most High gave them the kingdom, the way he gave it to Nebuchadnezzar, and the way he took it from him.

The nations are waiting for us to wake up, shake off our sins, and take our place as the kings and priests of the earth. The kingdom of men sits in the hands of the basest until the sons of God are manifested; the earnest expectation of the creature is for that day.

precepts.text: So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.
precepts.point: A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.” Paul draws the line: “So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.”

A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles. That which is born of the flesh stays flesh, and they that are in the flesh cannot please God. That is why Christ says, “Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” A man must be born of the Spirit to please God.

precepts.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
precepts.point: He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.” Paul says who those are: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

No condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus; and they are marked by how they walk, not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. He that hears his word and believes on him that sent him is passed from death unto life, and does not come into condemnation.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why: All this is stemming from Revelation 8:5, where Raphael cast the prayers of the saints into the earth and there were voices and thunderings and lightnings, which is evidence of when the Lord begins to answer our prayer in the midst of our speaking to him; this is taking us back to that time period and how we have to get to that point. “And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit,” So the Lord knows the mind of the Spirit. “because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.” That is what the Lord does: Christ makes intercession for us, the Holy Spirit, Christ, makes intercession for us, knowing what the will is.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 1

precepts.why: Paul explains how we can become faultless in this truth. “Who walk not after the flesh”: after guile, deceit, treachery and evil, “but after the Spirit”: the laws of God. That’s how we are found faultless, without condemnation; walk in the spirit.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

precepts.why: Add this to your arsenal. “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus”: why aren’t they condemned? Because no matter what they’ve done, the Most High said it’s done, it’s gone, I’ve forgiven him. You can’t even utter it before the Lord, but this brother or that sister did this; he don’t want to hear that.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 2

precepts.why: This is what he means by virgins. “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit”: who walk not after sin, but after the law in Christ. That is how we are a chaste virgin, because we are doing our best to walk in these laws, and this is how we are without fault before the throne.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”. The faithful Israelites of the first resurrection inherit with Christ. What the Father promised him in Psalms 2, he shares with them in Revelation 2: power over the nations and the rod of iron. The inheritance is why Christ can promise them what he received of his Father.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: That’s why another scripture says we are joint-heirs with Christ. “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”.
